name: Washington (L&I)
metric_note: Washington action levels are ambient outdoor temperature and vary by the clothing a worker is required to wear.
year_round_note: The July 2023 revision removed the May-September seasonal window. Requirements apply whenever the trigger is met.

thresholds.name: Action level, standard clothing
requirements: Sufficiently cool drinking water, 1 quart per worker per hour
Shade or other sufficient means of cooling, accessible at all times
Written Outdoor Heat Exposure Safety Program in force
Acclimatisation monitoring for new and returning workers over their first 14 days

thresholds.name: Action level, double-layer clothing
requirements: Same water, shade and program duties as the standard action level
Applies at a lower temperature because coveralls and jackets suppress evaporative cooling
thresholds.evidence_note: Clothing-dependent trigger. Site clothing type must be recorded for this to be defensible.

thresholds.name: Action level, vapour-barrier clothing
requirements: Full heat protection duties apply from 52°F for chemical-resistant suits and other vapour-barrier PPE
thresholds.evidence_note: The lowest statutory heat trigger in any US jurisdiction.

thresholds.name: High-heat procedures
requirements: Mandatory paid cool-down period of at least 10 minutes every 2 hours
Active observation of workers for signs and symptoms of heat illness
Effective communication and a designated emergency caller
thresholds.evidence_note: Cool-down periods are paid time and must be scheduled, not merely permitted.

thresholds.name: Extreme heat procedures
requirements: Mandatory paid cool-down period of at least 15 minutes every hour
Continued active observation and emergency readiness
thresholds.evidence_note: Break frequency roughly doubles at this threshold.
